newsitem.title: ROMANIA: Romania competition council probes Azomures sale.
newsitem.headline: Romania competition council probes Azomures sale.

text.p: Romania's main competition supervisor said on Friday it was investigating the the 51 percent privatisation of fertiliser maker Azomures SA, following complaints of alleged irregularities.

"Other bidders complained about the way in which the tender was organised," said Viorel Munteanu, president of the Competition Council, an autonomous body created to rule on fair competition as Romania moves towards a free market.

Munteanu said his Council would also look into a possible "economic concentration" in the fertiliser industry by Romanian trading company Euro Trading Chemicals SRL, which bought the Azomures stake from its former main holder the State Ownership Fund (FPS).
Euro also has majority stakes in another two local fertiliser makers.
"We are now assessing whether Euro Trading does indeed have a controlling position in the three companies," Munteanu said.
The government had asked police to investigate alleged irregularities in the Azomures deal.
Euro Trading officials have not been available for comment since the sale in February.
The Azomures sale aroused controversy, with the rival bidder, Omnimpex Chemicals SA local trader, complaining to the FPS that factors other than price had been considered.
The FPS said it had sold Euro Trading the Azomures shares at 90,000 lei each, without giving an overall purchasing price.
Azomures, which has a share capital of 209.5 billion lei, is a Bucharest stock exchange first-tier listing and has been traded actively ever since it joined the bourse last January.
Munteanu said the Council had 30 days to solve the complaints about the tender and five months to rule on the suspicions of a "concentration in the fertiliser sector".
Stock brokers said the Council's investigations were unlikely to affect trading in Azomures. They said the market might react when a report on its inquiry was issued.
Azomures closed Thursday at 1,360 lei, 160 up on the week.
